options.name: allow_development_packages
options.description: Enables or disables allowing the use of development (-devel) variants of pfSense packages when a package is required by specific API endpoints. Use of development packages is at your own risk.

options.name: allow_pre_releases
options.description: Enables or disables displaying pre-releases in available API updates. Pre-releases contain fixes and features that are currently under development and may not be fully stable. Use of pre-release versions is at your own risk.

options.name: allowed_interfaces
options.description: Sets the interfaces allowed to accept incoming API calls.

options.name: api_host
options.description: The hostname or IP address of the pfSense device.

options.name: api_key
options.description: An API key to use for authentication.

options.name: api_password
options.description: The password to authenticate with the pfSense API.

options.name: api_port
options.description: The port number of the pfSense API.

options.name: api_protocol
options.description: The protocol to use when connecting to the pfSense API.

options.name: api_username
options.description: The username to authenticate with the pfSense API.

options.name: auth_methods
options.description: Sets the API authentication methods allowed to authenticate API calls.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enables or disables the API. If set to `false`, the API will no longer respond to API requests and can only be re-enabled via webConfigurator.

options.name: expose_sensitive_fields
options.description: Enables or disables exposing sensitive fields in API responses. When enabled, sensitive fields such as passwords, private keys, and other sensitive data will be included in API responses.

options.name: ha_sync
options.description: Enables or disables syncing API settings to HA peers. When enabled, API settings from this host will automatically be synced to any hosts defined in `ha_sync_hosts`.

options.name: ha_sync_hosts
options.description: Set a list of IP addresses or hostnames to sync API settings to.

options.name: ha_sync_password
options.description: Sets the password to use when authenticating for HA sync processes. This must be the password for the user defined in `ha_sync_username` and must be the same on all hosts defined in `ha_sync_hosts`.

options.name: ha_sync_username
options.description: Sets the username to use when authenticating for HA sync processes. This user must be the present on all hosts defined in `ha_sync_hosts` and must hold the `page-all` privilege

options.name: ha_sync_validate_certs
options.description: Enables or disables certificate validation when syncing API configurations to HA sync peers. If enabled, all hosts defined in `ha_sync_hosts` must have their webConfigurator configured with a certificate trusted by this system. It is strongly recommended this be enabled at all times to help mitigate Man-in-the-Middle attacks.

options.name: hateoas
options.description: Enables or disables HATEOAS. Enabling HATEOAS will allow the API to include links to related resources in API responses. This is primarily useful for frontend web applications and self-navigating client scripts that integrate with HAL standards. Enabling HATEOAS may increase API response times, especially on systems with large configurations.

options.name: jwt_exp
options.description: Sets the amount of time (in seconds) JWTs are valid for.

options.name: keep_backup
options.description: Enables or disables keeping a persistent backup of the API configuration that can be used to restore the API configuration after package and systems updates.

options.name: log_level
options.description: Sets the log level for API logging. The log level determines the minimum severity of messages that should be logged.

options.name: log_successful_auth
options.description: Enables or disables logging of API authentication attempts that are successful. By default, only failed API authentication attempts are logged to prevent flooding the authentication logs. This field is only applicable when the API `login_protection` setting is enabled.

options.name: login_protection
options.description: Enables or disables Login Protection for API authentication. When enabled, Login Protection will monitor API attempts and temporarily block clients who fail API authentication too many times within a period of time. When disabled, Login Protection will not monitor API authentication but will continue to monitor webConfigurator and SSH logins (if configured). Login Protection can be configured globally in System > Advanced.

options.name: override_sensitive_fields
options.description: Specifies a list of fields (formatted as ModelName:FieldName) that should have their sensitive attribute overridden. Fields selected here will not be considered sensitive and will be included in API responses regardless of the `expose_sensitive_fields` setting.

options.name: read_only
options.description: Enables or disables read-only API access. If enabled, the API will only respond to GET requests and can only be disabled via webConfigurator.

options.name: represent_interfaces_as
options.description: Specifies how the API should represent interface names. Use `descr` to represent interface objects by their description name, use `id` to represent interface objects by their internal pfSense ID (e.g. wan, lan, opt1), or use `if` to represent interface objects by their real interface name (e.g. em0, igb1, bxe3).

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Whether to validate SSL certificates when connecting to the API.
